text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Road tolls may be scrapped, but the price of petrol could rise to make up for the difference.
- President Tudjman opens a newly erected Maslenica bridge.
- Serb National Party President Milan Dukic announces that his party will not take part in the coming elections, due to reservations he has his about their legality.
- Agroobrtnicka Banka becomes an outlet for the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) as part of the government's programme to grant loans to demobilised soldiers.
- Czech dairy PROM shows interest in dairy production investment in the area of Konavle, south of Dubrovnik.
- Total workforce 1.4 million in February, but employment in the real sector has shrunk by about 190,000 or 35 percent from 1990.
- Pre-election polls show Tudjman and HDZ in a commanding lead.
- The London-based European credit rating agency IBCA awards a long-term BBB- rating to Zagrebacka Banka.
- The kuna is just a step away from becoming convertible, Dubravko Radosevic, head of international relations at the central bank, says in an interview.
- Japanese bankers may come to Croatia in May to explore investment possibilities, says MP Djuro Njavro after a visit to Japan. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
